claims.statement: The download subsystem splits ownership so that JS owns task metadata, queue state, persistence, progress percentage and output file names, while Java owns byte transfer, MediaStore/app-directory writes, encoders and share intents — which is how the 'no image bytes in the JS heap' rule is preserved for queue downloads.

A queue task equals one output file (a 5-page illust enqueues 5 tasks, a ugoira or novel export enqueues 1), tasks carry per-kind ids (img_<illustId>_p<page>, ugoira_<illustId>_<format>, novel_<id>_<format>_<sig>), and enqueue is idempotent because drafts whose id already exists are skipped — combining with 'completed cannot be started' means a finished file must be deleted from the queue before it can be re-downloaded.

Queue transition legality is a closed rule set implemented by canStart/canPause/canStop and the start/pause/stop reducers: start re-queues queued|paused|stopped|failed and clears error but never touches completed or downloading (silent no-op), pause applies only to downloading, stop applies to queued|downloading|paused and zeroes progress while clearing bytesDone/bytesTotal/outputUri/error, and only the executor can set completed or failed.

The scheduler is a pure function over MAX_CONCURRENT (=1, single connection per task): it counts tasks already downloading, picks the earliest queued tasks by createdAt with original array index as tie-break up to the free slots, promotes them to downloading, and assigns each new run a runId one greater than its previous value.

A runId generation guard makes stale async callbacks inert: reportProgress, complete and fail are accepted only while the task is still downloading and the callback's runId matches, so progress or completion from a paused, stopped or deleted run can never move the task back; progress is clamped to 0–100 and byte counts are stored alongside it.

createDownloadManager is the orchestration shell over the pure core plus two injected seams (KV and DownloadExecutor): it debounce-persists every state change, warns instead of throwing when persistence fails, pumps the scheduler on enqueue/start/complete/fail/pause/stop/delete so a freed single slot immediately starts the next queued task, and asks the executor to suspend/cancel only for tasks whose status makes that meaningful.

Deletion cancels any selected in-flight task first, then (mode='files' only) deletes the outputUri of selected tasks that are completed, then removes the records; a failed file deletion is only warned about and the record is removed anyway, which is the accepted orphan-file trade-off behind 'delete files before records'.

The queue persists as one JSON document under the key download_queue_v1 shaped {version: 1, tasks: [...]}, written through a DownloadKV seam — native PictelioPrefs over the SharedPreferences file CapacitorStorage in production, IndexedDB in the web-core dev path — with a 300 ms debounce and serialized writes; flush() drains a pending debounce but currently has no production caller.

Restore is strict and loud: unparseable JSON, a schema-version mismatch or a non-array tasks field yields an empty queue plus a warning, each entry is revalidated so damaged records are dropped with a warning count, and a task that was downloading at process death is downgraded to paused with a warning; hydrate is one-shot/idempotent by design and never auto-starts restored work.

The queue document and its task field names are a persisted-format contract, not an internal detail: a schema-version bump without a migration path silently empties every installed user's queue, and normalizeTask rebuilds records from known field names and drops unknown ones, so renaming or retyping a persisted field turns existing records into dropped entries.

The literals CapacitorStorage and capacitor-storage_ are legacy user-data formats that must not be renamed; the prefs file also holds the queue key and the device-level setting keys, so renaming it would orphan every installed user's queue and settings.

System sharing is a JS selection step plus one native intent: the store collects outputUri values of selected completed tasks and throws a readable error when there is nothing to share or no sharer is registered, while ShareHelper keeps content:// URIs as-is, converts file:// through FileProvider (Android 7+ forbids leaking file://), picks ACTION_SEND vs ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE, grants read permission and resolves mime as explicit argument → content resolver → extension whitelist → application/octet-stream.

The Lynx bridge is thin and callback-based with no null contract: cb(value, "") on success and cb("", readable message) on failure with string arguments JSON-quoted by the callback layer (hence unquoteNativeString on the JS side); PictelioDownloader.start takes id, sourceUrl, fileName, kind, targetFormat, framesJson, payloadJson, dir in that order, progress is pull-mode via pollProgress returning "done/total" or "-1/0" when idle, and cancel returns "1"/"0".

Progress percentages are computed in JS, not in the native executor: a 300 ms interval polls the native progress snapshot, parses done/total into an integer percentage (clamped at 100) and suppresses unchanged values, then the queue core clamps to 0–100 and stores bytesDone/bytesTotal.

Native module lookup is deliberately lazy on first task use rather than at bundle evaluation: native modules are injected after the bundle evaluates, so an eager probe would decide 'missing' forever and disable the whole queue for the session; when the module is genuinely absent the first attempt warns once and fails the task explicitly instead of degrading silently.

The shipped Lynx executor cannot suspend a download while keeping its bytes: pause is implemented as the same native cancel as stop, so a paused task re-downloads from zero on the next start even though the queue record keeps its previous percentage until the rerun reports new values.

The still-image task path is PictelioDownloader.download → PixivImageLoader.loadFileWithProgress (cache-first, streaming, progress, cancellation — inheriting the mirror/Referer/UA semantics of the shared image core) → GallerySaver.saveFile, with one AtomicBoolean cancel token per task id registered only while in flight and cancel(id) returning false for unknown or finished tasks.

GallerySaver splits destinations by API level without ever requesting a runtime permission: on API ≥ 29 it writes to MediaStore.Images with RELATIVE_PATH "Pictures/Pictelio" using the IS_PENDING two-phase write and deletes the pending row when the byte copy fails; on API 28 (minSdk) it writes atomically into getExternalFilesDir(Pictures)/Pictelio with a best-effort MediaScannerConnection.scanFile and returns file:// with SaveResult.mediaStore = false. Names are not de-duplicated here because MediaStore 29+ appends " (1)" itself and the fallback path overwrites.

GallerySaver's sanitizeFileName is the Java second line of defence (path separators and control characters → "_", then trim; empty result is a readable failure) and the JS sanitizeNameSegment mirrors that replacement table exactly, with a cross-language contract test keeping the two in sync; both mime resolvers fall back asymmetrically on purpose (GallerySaver → image/jpeg, ShareHelper → application/octet-stream).

The ugoira export path is downloadUgoira (stream the official ZIP with the same cancel-aware progress core) → UgoiraExporter.export(format) into the app cache → GallerySaver.saveDownloadFile (MediaStore.Downloads, base Downloads/Pictelio; app-specific Downloads directory on API 28); frame timings arrive as framesJson and when that is missing or unparseable the exporter falls back to ZIP entry order with 100 ms per frame plus a warning, while an unknown format, a non-decodable frame or mismatched frame sizes raise a readable IOException.

All six ugoira encoders live in Java so frame bytes never enter the JS heap: zip copies the source ZIP, tar writes ustar headers from the ZIP central directory, apng reassembles PNG chunks (acTL/fcTL/fdAT, re-encoding non-PNG frames to PNG first), gif decodes frames and emits GIF89a with a fixed 216-colour palette plus LZW (pure JVM), webp compresses each frame with the device libwebp through Bitmap.compress and assembles the RIFF VP8X/ANIM/ANMF container in pure Java, and mp4 drives MediaCodec H.264 plus MediaMuxer while keeping its pure parts (ARGB→YUV420, frame rate, PTS) JVM-testable.

JS is the single source of truth for output file names: buildSaveFileName delegates to the default template Pictelio_{id} so the legacy single-page and _p<N> multi-page names are reproduced byte-for-byte, templates support {id}/{title}/{author}/{p} with {p} expanding to empty on single-page works (connector stripped) and an automatic _p<N> suffix when {p} is absent, unknown placeholders are kept verbatim and warned about once per name, values are sanitised with the Java-mirrored rule and truncated to 64 characters per segment and 120 for the final name with the extension preserved, and an empty or all-sanitised template falls back to the default with a warning.

Two device-level settings keys control naming — download_file_template (default Pictelio_{id}) and download_by_author_dir (default off) — and when enabled the sanitised author segment is appended after a fixed base (Pictures/Pictelio for still-image tasks and the direct gallery module, Downloads/Pictelio for non-image exports) with a missing author name degrading to the base plus a warning; both template and directory are snapshotted into the task at enqueue time, and Java only gained an optional subPath parameter whose empty value is byte-identical to the previous behaviour, so a template literal can never inject a path.

The ugoira export format is a global device-level setting: settings_ugoira_download_format accepts exactly gif, mp4, webp, apng, zip and tar (whitelist shared as downloadQueueCore.UGOIRA_FORMATS), defaults to zip, keeps the default with a warning when a persisted value is illegal, and is snapshotted into the task at enqueue so changing the setting never rewrites queued work — there is no per-image format.

The queue is device-local task state and is deliberately outside the WebDAV backup domain (BACKUP_DEVICE_KEYS), while the three download-related settings keys settings_ugoira_download_format, download_file_template and download_by_author_dir are declared in that backup domain.

The /downloads page is a secondary route (requiresAuth, topInset 'self') whose derived logic lives in a pure view model: tasks are grouped by illustId, an empty selection means 'all tasks' so the action bar doubles as a bulk control, start/pause/stop availability comes from canStart/canPause/canStop over the effective selection, delete is always available for a non-empty selection, share requires a completed task with an outputUri, the delete dialog offers the destructive 'delete files and records' branch only when a selected task has a deletable file, and the dialog registers with modalStack so system back closes it before leaving the page.

The /downloads page keeps two measured layout constraints: the bottom action bar is in normal flow rather than an absolute overlay because an overlaid bar did not receive taps in native LynxView, and the list is non-virtualized but uses the shared capped stagger (STAGGER_MAX_ITEMS = 8) so a long history cannot push later cards arbitrarily late; the shared FabAllowanceSpacer replaces a previously hand-tuned bottom height.

For the page, every tappable element carries an accessibility element flag and a label from the DOWNLOAD_A11Y_LABELS registry, and a source-level guard test asserts the registry is non-empty, unique, consumed key-for-key by the template, holds matching label/element counts, and pins the literal delete-action copy 删除文件与记录 / 仅清空记录.

The illust detail save entry points were converted from direct saving to enqueueing: single-page works enqueue one task, multi-page works open the page picker and enqueue the chosen pages, ugoira fetches metadata then enqueues one task with the global format, both read the naming template and author-directory settings at enqueue time, and the inline status is followed by a 'view downloads' jump to /downloads; the legacy saveIllustPages orchestrator and saveImageToGallery bridge remain tested but have no production caller left.

Novel exports ride the same queue as opaque tasks: kind 'novel' carries a serialized payloadJson the queue core never parses, the native path reports only coarse checkpoints (5 % before encoding, 90 % before saving, 100 % set by the queue on completion because encoding is not sliceable), and the novel 'already downloaded' state is derived from completed queue tasks rather than any separate persistence layer, so clearing the queue resets it.

Declared scope boundaries of the queue are: no background continuation (a process kill brings downloading tasks back as paused and nothing auto-resumes them; WorkManager-style continuation is a follow-up ticket), concurrency fixed at 1 with no segmented multi-thread download, no list-level cross-work batch download (batch means batch over queued tasks), no per-image format, and no iOS (Android-only project).

Verification is partial by declaration: the mp4 MediaCodec path and the webp per-frame Bitmap.compress path are not covered by the JVM/Robolectric encoder tests and are flagged for device acceptance, real-device download and sharing smoke runs are still pending, and the E2E ticket T14 is still open with no download spec present under the android-e2e suite.

The bridge's Capacitor half is history: with the WebView client removed only the Lynx modules (PictelioDownloader/PictelioGallery/PictelioShare) and their JS adapters remain, and the contract test that once asserted a matching Capacitor plugin signature now records that the assertion was deleted with the WebView client while the Lynx and Java deep-module assertions keep running.
